newsitem.title: USA: Five TV spots get first-ever primetime emmy nods.
newsitem.headline: Five TV spots get first-ever primetime emmy nods.

text.p: Five TV ads were nominated Thursday for primetime Emmys as the television industry for the first time formally recognised the entertainment value of commercials.

Sheila Manning, a governor of the Academy of Television Arts & Sciences, said the final five were whittled down from a batch of 237 spots submitted primarily by advertising agencies and production companies.

"I think personally that commercials are far and away the best thing on television," said Ms. Manning, who owns a commercial casting company in Los Angeles and admits she is not completely unbiased. "It just became time for the Academy to recognise commercials. Commercials have come so far in the last five to seven years."

The nominees included two spots created for Levis wide-leg jeans by ad agency Foote Cone & Belding, a unit of True North Communications. Two ads by director Joe Pytka -- one for the HBO cable network and another for Nike -- were among the nominees.
Manning said the criteria was the same used for selecting nominees in such categories as the best show or best miniseries -- production, story line, direction and talent.

"What's happened is with the advent of the remote control that commercials -- as shows -- have become far more sophisticated, forgetting technology," she said. "They have only 30 seconds to give the complete story."
The 49th Annual Primetime Emmy Awards ceremony will take place on Sept. 14.
